name: Stacked-tower vs standalone-prototype EUI basis
detail: channel(s) below their as-modelled floor: office, retail, hotel (office 71.1 vs floor 100; retail 75.4 vs floor 80; hotel 178.3 vs floor 180). The locked bands come from STANDALONE prototypes; these channels are floors inside one tower, where most of the envelope is interior partition to other conditioned space and the plant is shared and centrally sized. A lower EUI is the physically expected direction. NO THRESHOLD HAS BEEN CHANGED -- whether the standalone band remains a valid PASS criterion for a stacked-tower channel is a decision to be taken explicitly. CORRECTED 2026-07-31 (re-derived from code, not taken on faith): the Leg-2 office precedent (135 [100-200], job 1054800) is computed on ALL FUELS, not restricted to any single meter -- _eui_from_sql() (Leg2_2-split/Step8_docs/3rdJ_08_simulation_2split_agg.py:333-345) calls calculate_eui() (Leg2_2-split/Step8_docs/eSim_bem_utils_3J/plotting.py:257-350), which sums the SQL 'End Uses (By Subcategory)' table over ALL fuel columns, excluding only m3 units (water) -- gas is in it. The Electricity:Facility / office_elec restriction lives on the DIURNAL path (Leg2_2-split/Step9_docs/3rdJ_09_activityDrivenLoads_2split.py:99-110) and never feeds the EUI at all (contrast :124-158). The real, larger discrepancy is elsewhere: the Leg-2 'office' EUI is a TOWER EUI, not a channel EUI -- its `unit` column literally reads 'tower' (Leg2_2-split/Step9_docs/outputs_step9/step9_eui_by_channel.csv, row office,all,tower,252,172.7), and calculate_eui() returns the energy and area of the WHOLE model. Leg-2 therefore never validated an office CHANNEL -- Leg-3 produces the project's first per-channel EUI.

name: Envelope-exposure mechanism test (T9-3) vs band-floor gap
detail: median exposure_ratio by channel: hotel (0.325) < office (0.382) < retail (0.467) (n=56 cells). Median gap to band floor: office -28.9%; retail -5.7%; hotel -0.9%. Spearman(exposure_ratio, signed gap-to-floor) pooled over the 3 banded channels, rho = -0.171 (p=0.026, n=168). PREDICTED office < retail < hotel (least-exposed channel = largest negative gap); MEASURED hotel < office < retail -- the prediction is CONTRADICTED, in 56/56 cells (hotel is the LEAST-exposed of the three, not the most, and sits CLOSEST to its floor, not furthest) -- the negative pooled rho is the wrong sign for the 'stacked channel buries the envelope' story. TESTED AND REFUTED: the 3 EUI FAIL gates above are not explained by this mechanism and remain unexplained defects. LIMIT: geometry varies only between the Tall and SuperTall archetypes in this campaign, so exposure_ratio takes only 2 distinct values per channel -- the per-cell rho moves because EUI re-orders across scenarios, not because exposure does. The inference is therefore over 2 geometries, not 56 independent ones.

name: Tower-level EUI, both bases (context, NOT scored PASS/FAIL)
detail: ABUPS gross basis (site_energy_GJ / total_building_area_m2, all 56 cells): median 100.4 kWh/m2/yr (range 90.8-115.3). Tenant-CFA-summed basis (sum of the 4 tenant channels' own energy / sum of their CFA, 56 cells): median 110.3 kWh/m2/yr (range 99.7-127.3). The Leg-2 office precedent band [100-200] (central 135, from NECB2020/90.1-2019 DOE-PNNL literature) is cited here as CONTEXT ONLY, never as a PASS/FAIL criterion. Note the two are different objects: the band is literature and is sound; 172.7 is the value Leg-2 MEASURED against it, and it is that measured number -- not the band -- that is inflated by a factor of ~1.706x by a calculate_eui() defect (Leg2_2-split/Step8_docs/eSim_bem_utils_3J/plotting.py:293-299 filters on TableName without ever filtering ReportName, so the same-named 'End Uses By Subcategory' table from the DemandEndUseComponentsSummary report -- which is in WATTS -- gets summed in as if it were kWh); 172.7 / 1.706 = 101.2, within ~1% of the ~100 kWh/m2/yr measured here on the same tower once that defect is removed. Leg2_2-split/ was read only, never modified; correcting the Leg-2 number is a user decision outside this task's scope.

name: Weekday residential occupancy: evening (17-22 h) above midday (11-14 h), injected cells
detail: 52/52 injected cells; evening/midday ratio median 2.41 (range 1.56-7.37); the un-injected NECB baseline sits at 0.22 (midday-dominant, argmax 09 h) -- see S9-INJECTION. Deliberately NOT scored on a mean hour: AT_HOME occupancy is near-antipodal (maximum overnight while people sleep at home, minimum around 10 h), so R = 0.267 and the mean hour wanders over almost the whole clock across behaviourally identical cells. The doc's 'resid 15-22 h' describes the evening RISE, and that is what this measures.

name: Residential injection changes the occupancy SHAPE, not just its level
detail: NECB code baseline: evening/midday occupancy ratio 0.22 (midday-dominant, argmax 9 h). GSS-injected cells: 2.41 (range 1.56-7.37, argmax 4 h). The injection flips the channel from midday-dominant to evening-dominant -- a change of SHAPE, which a level-only rescaling of the code schedule could not produce. This is the cleanest sim-side evidence that the residential channel carries behaviour and not merely a magnitude, and it is exactly the claim the thesis rests on.

name: Residential evening ENERGY peak (the Legs 1-2 headline)
detail: NOT REPRODUCIBLE IN LEG 3, by construction. Residential energy peaks at 12.13 h (circular mean, R = 0.285), not in the evening, because OD-7D leaves residential lights and plug loads on the flat NECB baseline -- the very loads that produced the evening peak in Legs 1 and 2. The OCCUPANCY still shows the evening rise (see S9-PEAK-residential), so the behavioural signal is intact upstream; it simply has no route into energy. This is D-20 at its sharpest, and it belongs in the manuscript: any Leg-3 claim about residential evening ENERGY demand would be unsupported by this model.

name: Energy-vs-occupancy peak lag per channel (D-20 evidence)
detail: office 0.26 h; retail 0.53 h; hotel 5.07 h; residential 10.56 h. The three commercial channels modulate People + Lights + Equipment, so their energy timing tracks their occupancy. Residential modulates People only (OD-7D), so its energy timing is set by the flat NECB baseline instead. That gap is the asymmetry D-20 predicted, here as a measured number rather than an argument.
